chainLevelFindings: Constructor args go in `data`; `code` must be the untouched PolkaVM blob. Appending args to the blob makes the runtime reject the deploy with Revive::CodeRejected.
Contract-side value uses EVM decimals (1e18) while extrinsic value uses planck (1e10). Divide a contract-side amount by 1e8 to get the planck to transfer.
ReviveApi.upload_code accepted the 126,233-byte ArbitratorCore blob (deposit 16.6 PAS), so blob size was never the constraint.
ReviveApi.balance returns a U256 as four little-endian u64 limbs, not a bigint.
A contract revert arrives as a SUCCESSFUL dispatch whose return flags have bit 0 set; the payload is the custom-error selector.
Block time is ~2s, and signAndSubmit waits for finalization (~12 blocks per extrinsic), so phase windows must be sized in blocks accordingly.
